signals.notes: Direction stated relative to PRICE: a cheaper USD mechanically raises the price a non-US buyer can pay for USD-denominated copper. Fed nominal BROAD trade-weighted index (Jan-2-2006=100): Aug-2025 120.5758 [Federal Reserve H.10 monthly, release dated 2026-08-03]; Aug-2026 118.9028 [TradingEconomics relay of the Fed series, 2026-08-28] = -1.39% over twelve months. Strength is low deliberately: the move is 1.39% against a +46.63% price move. BASIS: Fed nominal broad TRADE-WEIGHTED index, NOT DXY (a six-currency bilateral basket ~58% euro). DXY readings (98.55 on 2026-08-22, above 99 later that week) are context only and were NOT substituted for this row. Required series macro.broad-usd-index is MISSING (connector federal-reserve-broad-usd declared, no eligible immutable vintage at decision time); this row does not satisfy it and cannot lift sufficiency.

The opposing fact, emitted separately rather than averaged into the row above (MODULE_RULES section 8). On the last FULLY PUBLISHED Federal Reserve primary observation the broad dollar is UNCHANGED over eleven months: Aug-2025 120.5758 vs Jul-2026 120.5970 = +0.02% [Federal Reserve H.10 monthly nominal broad dollar index, release dated 2026-08-03]. The entire -1.39% twelve-month decline claimed by the row above sits in the single Aug-2026 stub, which is a secondary relay and not yet a published Fed monthly figure. Anyone treating the dollar as a live copper driver in this run is leaning on one unpublished month.

MODULE_RULES section 4a result, emitted so no downstream orb re-attempts the attribution. NO sourced sensitivity exists for copper's price response to the Fed nominal broad trade-weighted dollar, so ZERO of the observed +46.63% (+US$2.11/lb, 12m to 2026-08-28) twelve-month move is attributed to the dollar: 0% explained, 100% residual. Three candidate coefficients were found and ALL THREE were REFUSED on basis grounds, not applied: (1) a 'cross-border demand elasticity of -0.8 to -1.2' [discoveryalert.com.au, 2026] is an elasticity of demand QUANTITY with respect to effective price, not a price-to-dollar sensitivity; (2) '15% DXY decline coincided with a 167% copper rise 2008-2011' [same source] is an N=1 co-movement measured on the DXY bilateral basket, not a coefficient on the broad trade-weighted index; (3) current DXY levels are a different index from the required macro.broad-usd-index row and were not substituted for it. Inverse arithmetic only, offered as a reductio and NOT as an attribution: for the dollar alone to explain the move, copper's elasticity to the broad dollar would have to be 46.63 / 1.3875 = about -33.6. No sourced coefficient exists to compare that against.

Direction stated relative to PRICE: higher real rates raise the carry cost of financing physical copper inventory and of sanctioning new capacity, and tighten conditions for the construction and grid spending copper is consumed by. US 10-year REAL (TIPS) yield 2.36% at 2026-08-28, up 0.54pp (+54bp) over twelve months from about 1.82% [TradingEconomics, 2026-08-28]; cross-checked at 2.34% on 2026-08-26 [ConvexTrade]; the 2026-07-23 10-year TIPS auction cleared at 2.438%, the highest at auction for this term since October 2008 [Tipswatch, 2026-07-23]. BASIS: 10-year REAL yield. The 10-year NOMINAL yield is 4.69% (2026-08-28) and the implied breakeven about 2.33pp (derived); nominal, real and breakeven are three different bases and no coefficient measured on one may be applied to another. Required series macro.us-10y-real-yield is UNAVAILABLE - no connector claims it; treasury-real-yields-gold exists but is bound to the Gold profile and was NOT borrowed.

MODULE_RULES section 4a result. NO sourced sensitivity exists for copper's price response to the US 10-year real yield, so nothing is attributed: 0% of the +46.63% (+US$2.11/lb) twelve-month move is explained by real yields. Worse than unexplained, the SIGN IS ADVERSE - real yields ROSE 54bp across the same window in which copper ROSE 46.63%, so on the transmission mechanism described this driver SUBTRACTED from the move and the residual is at least 100%, plausibly more. This is the finding and not a caveat: a price mostly unexplained by its named macro drivers means the engine does not know what moved it, which caps conviction under sections 11 and 12. Falsifier for this orb's own read: if real yields rise another 25bp and copper rises with them again, the real-rate channel is not operating on copper in this regime and the Headwind mark should be downgraded to Neutral rather than defended.

Direction stated relative to PRICE: policy that keeps real rates high sustains the inventory-financing and investment headwind described in the real-yields cluster. At the 2026-07-28/29 FOMC nine members voted to hold the target range at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent and THREE dissented preferring a 25bp INCREASE [Federal Reserve, FOMC minutes 28-29 July 2026]. A hold whose only dissents want to hike is a hawkish-leaning hold, not a pause on the way down. No sourced copper/policy-rate sensitivity exists; this row is DIRECTION ONLY and attributes none of the observed price move.

The opposing fact, emitted separately and linked rather than averaged away (MODULE_RULES section 8). Market commentary describes DXY falling to 98.55 on 2026-08-22, its lowest since May, on a Treasury buyback and a 9-3 Fed split, with softer growth and cooling inflation read as pointing to eventual Fed cuts that would weigh on the dollar [Vantage Markets, 2026-08-24 - unvintaged, secondary]. That is the transmission channel through which easier policy would help copper, and it points the OPPOSITE way from the hawkish-hold row. Note the basis: this is commentary on DXY, a bilateral six-currency basket, NOT the Fed broad trade-weighted index, and it is a market-expectation narrative rather than a policy print. This rates-policy cluster therefore holds both a bearish and a bullish row and is correctly a contradiction, never conviction-eligible.

USD/CLP about 913.67 at 2026-08-28, the Chilean peso stronger by 5.02% over twelve months, 52-week range 850.90-983.38 [Investing.com and valutafx quotes, 2026-08-28 - unvintaged, secondary]. Mechanism: a stronger producer currency raises Chilean miners' local cost base measured in USD, which is mildly cost-supportive for price. Direction is NEUTRAL on purpose and this row carries NO causal vote, because the CLP is a copper-linked currency - its strength over this window is largely an EFFECT of the copper rally rather than a cause, so using it to explain that rally would be circular. Chilean mine output, costs and disruptions belong to commodity-supply and are not duplicated here.

Explicit non-emission, recorded so the absence is visible rather than silent. The COPPER profile lists the energy-transition structural bid among its macro lenses, but the quantified grid, EV and data-centre demand bridge is the required series copper-energy-transition-demand, whose causal owner is commodity-demand-inventory (MODULE_RULES section 8) - and that orb recorded it NOT ASSESSABLE (copper-energy-transition-demand-not-assessable). Emitting a bullish energy-transition vote here would be the same fact voting twice, off a base the causal owner says it cannot measure. This orb therefore emits ZERO quantified energy-transition demand signal and attributes none of the +46.63% move to it.

Explicit non-emission. Gold's safe-haven and geopolitical-demand lens does not transfer to copper: copper carries no monetary-hedge bid, so a geopolitical event reaches the copper price only by restricting physical flow. Dated trade restrictions, export bans, sanctions, chokepoints and rerouting are the exclusive jurisdiction of commodity-supply-security, which has already emitted sixteen rows covering US Section 232, the DRC concentrate export ban, Indonesia, Russia exchange ineligibility, Panama and Peru. This orb emits no geopolitical-risk vote and attributes none of the observed move to one.
